assumptions.referenceTeam: Two full-time people: one gameplay programmer and one 2D artist-designer, with separate outsourcing budgets for audio, localization and QA.

teamVariants.solo: Use an 18-month ceiling and hold the full game to one bay and one season.
teamVariants.threeToFourPeople: Spend added capacity first on tools, accessibility, QA and store production rather than a new gameplay loop.

portfolioAudit.shortlistMeaning: Six concepts were selected for deeper comparison under the current team, platform and schedule assumptions. The other 147 were not declared duplicates or rejected products.

method.scoreScale: 1-5, where 5 is strongest for the stated reference-team assumption
method.caveat: Weighted totals are pre-prototype decision heuristics, not success probabilities, sales forecasts or measured market shares. Small score differences are treated as ties and can be reversed by measured team strengths.

ratingRationale.silentTenSecondClarity: Wave direction, line tension and the three input responses may be visible in a silent clip; this has not been user-tested.
ratingRationale.systemicContentLeverage: Behavior profiles, signal combinations and later weather can vary play without handcrafted maps.
ratingRationale.smallTeamProductionControl: One temporary fish, one bay and a fixed-seed baseline can test the core before final art or content.
ratingRationale.repeatedDecisionDifferentiation: The recurring decision is signal interpretation and tension control, not fish hit-point depletion or collection.
ratingRationale.marketAdjacency: Fishing games show adjacent paid audiences, but the available examples are 3D, social or online and do not directly validate this mechanic.

candidates.mainRisk: If players can reel continuously or line feel is ordinary, the differentiator disappears and only the fishing theme remains.

ratingRationale.silentTenSecondClarity: The heat changes can be previewed, but the difference is likely to require reading a numeric table.
ratingRationale.systemicContentLeverage: Vessel conditions, irreversible placement and four heat-air actions combine without new maps.
ratingRationale.smallTeamProductionControl: One kiln, one vessel per zone and four actions can test the core without real-time physics.
ratingRationale.repeatedDecisionDifferentiation: Players jointly correct three temperatures and one shared oxygen value on an irreversible timeline.
ratingRationale.marketAdjacency: Potion Craft and the broader simulation sample are adjacent signals for visible process play, not direct evidence for this kiln rule.

candidates.mainRisk: The player may not see the appeal before understanding the temperature and oxygen table.

ratingRationale.silentTenSecondClarity: Exact-number boards and lock-or-compound outcomes can be shown, though the idle context needs explanation.
ratingRationale.systemicContentLeverage: Board sizes and indivisible number bundles can produce combinatorial sessions.

ratingRationale.marketAdjacency: Incremental and desktop-companion interest is visible, but paid positioning is uncertain.

ratingRationale.silentTenSecondClarity: A stroke becoming a street, wall or yard is the highest-rated single-scene transformation in the internal review.
ratingRationale.systemicContentLeverage: Stroke grammar and resident constraints can produce different layouts.
ratingRationale.smallTeamProductionControl: Stroke recognition, deterministic previews and resident pathfinding must all feel reliable.

ratingRationale.marketAdjacency: Tiny Glade is only adjacent evidence for low-pressure creation, not proof of paid replay demand here.

candidates.mainRisk: Shareable scenes may not translate into paid replay motivation.

ratingRationale.marketAdjacency: The adjacent audience is broad but no close paid comparison validates the rule.

sixWeekScope.deliverable: One temporary visual, one behavior profile, three signals, three inputs, line break, reel-continuously baseline and behavior logging.
Silent ten-second clip, three-minute catch loop, early test with ten target users and one screen-feedback revision.
Three behavior profiles using the same temporary art, an eight-to-ten-minute expedition, instant retry and iterative testing with ten external users.
Keep-or-release choice pair connected to one visible variable in the next expedition; no weather, bait, sharing, relationship or grace events.
Content freeze, fresh 20-30-person final test and log analysis; no new fish, narrative, art or rule revision before the verdict.

validationGates.pass: At least 7 identify the core action and at least 5 describe the same differentiator.
At least 14 describe it as fishing where signals change reeling, releasing and rod angle.

validationGates.sample: For every behavior profile, 30 attempts per policy on the same preregistered seed set.
validationGates.attemptDenominator: All attempts in each policy; failed catches remain in the denominator.
validationGates.eventDefinition: Compare a preregistered reel-continuously policy against a preregistered signal-responsive policy, using identical seeds and attempt counts.
validationGates.catchRateEquivalenceBand: An absolute catch-rate difference of 5 percentage points or less.
validationGates.pass: Signal-responsive play is at least 20 percentage points higher in catch rate, or within the 5-point equivalence band has at least 25 percent lower median catch time.
After three attempts, at least 70 percent explain two signals without help, change input on the next matching signal, and intentionally release line at least once.

validationGates.eventDefinition: Starting another expedition from the result screen without a moderator prompt.
validationGates.pass: At least 40 percent start a second expedition.
At least three behavior profiles or situations favor observably different input sequences.
At least 70 percent predict the next-expedition effect of keeping or releasing, and neither choice exceeds 80 percent.
validationGates.failureAction: Remove or reduce the ecology layer without rejecting the fishing core.

publicDemoGate.prerequisite: The six-week core has passed and a 12-16-week vertical slice is complete; the public demo is the behavioral validation of that slice.
publicDemoGate.preregistration: Fix acquisition channels, measurement window, sample floor and event definitions before release.
publicDemoGate.behaviorPass: All three: 60 percent reach the core loop within five minutes, 40 percent finish the demo, and 25 percent of finishers immediately restart.
publicDemoGate.storeInterest: Record wishlist conversion with unique store-page visitors as the denominator; set a numeric target before release using an existing portfolio or channel baseline.
publicDemoGate.creatorResponse: Record actual demo runs and published coverage with outreach contacts as the denominator; set a numeric target before outreach.

businessGate.breakEvenFormula: ((development cost + marketing cost) * 1.2) / conservative net revenue per copy
businessGate.pass: Do not approve full production if the conservative scenario cannot reach break-even.

fullProductionApprovalRule: Approve only when demo behavior and the business gate both pass, and at least one preregistered external-demand gate—store interest or creator response—also passes.
coreStopRule: All three core-discard gates must pass. The week-2 screen-and-rule revision is the first revision. If the week-6 verdict fails, allow one final core-only revision of at most two weeks and retest on a fresh sample. Failure after that rejects only the Goraebada hypothesis.

fallback.name: 불숨 도깨비가마
fallback.twoWeekTest: One kiln, one vessel per lower-middle-upper zone and four actions; separately test ten-second comprehension, the necessity of numeric manipulation and voluntary restart.
useWhen: The team is measurably stronger at turn-based numeric systems than real-time feel and animation.
The fishing hypothesis is rejected after at most two core revisions.
fallback.ifFallbackFails: Rescore the remaining candidates rather than automatically entering a six-week kiln build.

games.caveat: Paid 3D action and co-op game; not direct evidence for a 2D single-player signal-reading mechanic.
Paid social and online game; its reviews do not establish demand for a solo product.
Adjacent evidence for a visible 2D process simulation, not proof for fishing controls.
Adjacent evidence for a low-pressure creative PC audience, not the same core loop.

steamReviewSnapshot.caveat: Submitted reviews are not copies sold, revenue or total players. The examples are retrospectively selected, have different time in market and do not prove mechanic-level causation.
